subject: Switchboard telemetry handoff & implementation action plan
messages:
From: Taylor Nguyen <taylor@switchboard.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>
Cc: Jared Lin <jared.lin@switchboard.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Feb 2027 19:18:00 -0500
Subject: Observability kickoff & next steps

Hi Camila,

Thanks again for the demo earlier — Switchboard is excited to move forward with Redwood for inference telemetry and alerts. We want to align on the implementation plan for dashboards, tracing hooks, and alert routing so our SREs can start instrumenting before the integration window in late March.

High-level asks from our side:
- A draft runbook we can slot into our incident playbooks
- Recommended tracing hook locations (API ingress, model gateway, prefix cache)
- Alert routing proposal: which signals should go to on-call vs. async ticketing

Can the Redwood team share a concise onboarding checklist and a proposed two-week implementation timeline? Also looping Jared (SRE) for technical context.

Best,
Taylor
Product Ops | Switchboard, Inc.
(t) 415-555-0199

(attachment: initial_scope_switchboard.pdf (PDF, 95KB))

From: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>
To: Taylor Nguyen <taylor@switchboard.com>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 11 Feb 2027 09:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Observability kickoff & next steps

Taylor — appreciate the clear asks. Attaching a concise checklist and a runbook template to get us started. Quick proposal below for the two-week implementation window and owners:

Week 0 (prep) — Discovery & network/credentials
- Owner: Neha (Customer Success)
- Deliverables: API endpoints list, network allowlist, expected traffic profile

Week 1 — Instrumentation & tracing hooks
- Owner: Evelyn (Solutions Eng)
- Tasks: Insert tracing calls at API ingress, model gateway, and batch worker boundaries; validate spans and sampling rates

Week 2 — Dashboards, alerts, and runbook integration
- Owner: Camila (Onboarding PM) / Evelyn
- Tasks: Create per-route latency/cost dashboards, define error taxonomy, map alerts to teams (on-call vs. ticketing), deliver runbook draft

As for signals we typically recommend putting on-call alerts for:
- End-to-end latency P95 above SLA threshold for 5+ minutes
- Model OOM or inference process crash
- Error-rate spikes (5xxs) that cross a 2% delta over baseline

Everything else (rate-limit warnings, degraded throughput) we route to async channels to avoid noise.

I attached: switchboard_onboarding_checklist.pdf, redwood_runbook-template.md, and a quick alert-routing spreadsheet. Can you confirm access to the Drive link below? If that looks good we can lock calendar slots for the 1-week instrumentation sprint the week of Mar 22.

Thanks,
Camila Reyes
Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference
camila@redwood.com | +1 650-555-0147

(attachments: switchboard_onboarding_checklist.pdf; redwood_runbook-template.md; alert-routing-proposal.xlsx)

From: Taylor Nguyen <taylor@switchboard.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>
Cc: Jared Lin <jared.lin@switchboard.com>, Procurement <procurement@switchboard.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Feb 2027 08:26:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Observability kickoff & next steps

Camila — this is great, thanks. A few clarifications from Jared (copied):

> From Jared Lin (SRE):
> For tracing, our current agent samples at 1% globally but can be bumped per-route. We want to ensure the model gateway spans are correlated to request IDs to avoid orphaned traces. Also, can Redwood recommend a default sampling rate for token-level spans?

Also attaching procurement — they may need a short SOW/statement of work that outlines the 2-week engagement and deliverables for approval. Can you provide that?

On scheduling: week of Mar 22 works but our release freeze is Mar 25–28; could we target Mar 29–Apr 9 for the instrumentation sprint instead?

Best,
Taylor

(attachment: sb_internal_arch.png (PNG, 450KB))

From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
To: Taylor Nguyen <taylor@switchboard.com>, Jared Lin <jared.lin@switchboard.com>, Procurement <procurement@switchboard.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 17 Feb 2027 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Observability kickoff & next steps — SOW + technical notes

Hi all — looping in Markus from our Solutions & Delivery team to confirm the SOW language and address Jared's tracing questions.

Quick answers / commitments: 
- Token-level spans: we typically recommend a 0.5% sampling rate for per-token spans for high-volume production traffic; bump to 2–5% in staging or for targeted routes. We'll include a small kernel of token-span examples in the runbook to show expected span payloads and sampling knobs.
- Request ID correlation: Redwood adds request_id to all span metadata by default when the header is present. We'll provide a short middleware snippet you can drop into the model gateway to ensure request_id propagation.
- SOW: attached draft SOW outlines a 2-week engagement, deliverables (checklist, runbook, dashboards, alert routing sheet), and acceptance criteria. We priced this as an engagement add-on scoped to 20 hours of Redwood engineering time.

Proposed timeline (final):
- Prep / credential exchange: by Mar 22
- Instrumentation sprint: Mar 29–Apr 9
- Runbook & dashboards delivered: Apr 12
- Hand-off review & closeout: Apr 15

Next steps for Switchboard:
1) Confirm instrumentation sprint window (Mar 29–Apr 9)
2) Confirm SOW and PO process with procurement
3) Provide API endpoints and ephemeral test credentials to Neha

If you confirm today I will send the finalized SOW and a calendar invite template for the sprint kickoff.

Thanks,
Markus Klein
Director, Solutions & Delivery | Redwood Inference
markus_klein@redwood.com

(attachment: SB_Redwood_SOW_draft.docx (DOCX, 26KB))
